functionalRequirement: System shall automatically update the available quantity of each medicine after a sale is completed.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The inventory system must accurately update medicine quantities for 100% of completed sales with zero discrepancies between recorded sales and inventory changes.
identifiedNFRs.justification: The FR requires precise tracking of medicine quantities, necessitating complete accuracy in inventory updates.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The inventory update must complete within 500 milliseconds after sale confirmation for 99% of transactions.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Automatic updates should occur promptly to maintain real-time inventory accuracy and prevent potential overselling.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The inventory update mechanism must have a failure rate of less than 0.01%, with automatic retry capabilities for failed updates.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Inventory accuracy is critical for medicine sales, requiring high reliability to prevent stock discrepancies.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: Inventory update operations must be restricted to authenticated sales processes and authorized personnel, with all changes logged for audit purposes.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Medicine inventory represents valuable assets requiring protection from unauthorized modifications.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The inventory update module must include automated tests that verify correct quantity calculations for at least 95% of possible sales scenarios.
identifiedNFRs.justification: The automatic nature of updates requires high testability to ensure continued correct operation as the system evolves.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The inventory system must support batch updates for bulk sales and returns, handling at least 1,000 items in a single transaction without performance degradation.
identifiedNFRs.justification: While the FR mentions individual sales, the system should scale to accommodate various sales volumes and scenarios.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The system must implement concurrency controls to prevent race conditions when multiple sales of the same medicine occur simultaneously, ensuring inventory accuracy is maintained.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Medicine inventory requires safe integration with the sales process to prevent critical errors in stock levels that could affect patient care.

identifiedNFRs.justification: Complete representation of all available slots is essential for the calendar view to fulfill its core purpose.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The calendar view must load and display all available appointment slots within 2 seconds, even when displaying data for up to 50 healthcare providers simultaneously.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The calendar interface must use color coding and clear visual indicators to distinguish between available, booked, and unavailable time slots, with a legend explaining these indicators.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The calendar must support navigation between days, weeks, and months with no more than 2 clicks or interactions per navigation action.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Easy navigation is essential for users to find available appointment slots across different time periods.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The calendar view must maintain 99.9% accuracy in reflecting real-time availability, with automatic updates at intervals of no more than 30 seconds.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Real-time accuracy is crucial to prevent double bookings and ensure users see current availability.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The calendar view must restrict access to provider availability information based on user roles, with authentication required for viewing sensitive scheduling details.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Provider schedules may contain sensitive information requiring appropriate access controls.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The calendar component must be implemented as a reusable module that can be updated independently from other system components, with documented APIs for integration.
identifiedNFRs.justification: A modular approach ensures the calendar view can be maintained and enhanced without affecting other system functions.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The calendar view must support customizable time slot intervals ranging from 5 minutes to 4 hours to accommodate different appointment types across various healthcare specialties.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Different healthcare providers may require different appointment durations based on their specialty and services.

identifiedNFRs.justification: The search must correctly implement all the specified criteria to fulfill its core purpose.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The property search must return results within 3 seconds for queries that may return up to 1000 properties, even during peak usage periods with 500 concurrent users.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Quick search response is essential for a good user experience in property search applications.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The search function must utilize database indexing on all searchable fields to optimize query performance, with query execution plans that execute in under 1 second for 95% of searches.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Efficient resource utilization is necessary to handle potentially complex property search queries.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The search interface must provide autocomplete suggestions for location fields after the user types 3 or more characters, with suggestions appearing within 500ms.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The search results must be sortable by at least 5 different criteria (e.g., price, date listed, size) with clear visual indicators of the current sort order.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Sorting options are essential for users to organize property search results according to their preferences.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The search functionality must maintain 99.95% uptime during business hours (8am-8pm local time), with degraded performance acceptable outside these hours only during scheduled maintenance.
identifiedNFRs.justification: High availability is crucial for property search functionality as it's a core feature of the system.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The search function must sanitize all user inputs to prevent SQL injection attacks, with input validation for all search parameters before query execution.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Search functionality typically involves user input that must be secured against potential injection attacks.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The search algorithm must be implemented in a separate service layer with documented APIs, allowing for future modifications to search logic without affecting the user interface.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Separating search logic improves maintainability as search algorithms may need optimization or enhancement over time.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The search functionality must support the addition of new search criteria without requiring more than 8 hours of development effort per new criterion.
identifiedNFRs.justification: The system should be adaptable to include additional property search criteria as business needs evolve.

identifiedNFRs.justification: The FR requires precise calculation of charges based on multiple variables, necessitating complete functional correctness.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The system must calculate modification charges and display new fares within 2 seconds of receiving all required inputs, even during peak loads of 1000 concurrent users.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Quick calculation and display of fares is essential for a smooth user experience when making modifications.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: Payment processing through the payment gateway must complete within 5 seconds for 95% of transactions and within 10 seconds for 99.5% of transactions.
identifiedNFRs.justification: The FR includes payment processing which requires efficient time behavior to maintain user satisfaction.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The system must display new fares in a format that clearly differentiates between original fare, modification charges, and total amount due, with appropriate currency symbols and decimal places.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Clear presentation of fare information is crucial for users to understand the financial impact of their modifications.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The system must maintain 99.9% uptime for the modification and payment processing functions, with scheduled maintenance occurring only during off-peak hours.
identifiedNFRs.justification: The FR involves financial transactions that require high availability to ensure users can make modifications when needed.

identifiedNFRs.justification: The FR includes payment processing which requires strong security measures to protect sensitive financial information.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The system must maintain an audit log of all modification charges and payment transactions, recording user ID, timestamp, modification details, and transaction ID for a minimum of 3 years.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Financial transactions require accountability and traceability for both business and regulatory purposes.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The fare calculation module must be implemented as a separate component with well-defined interfaces, allowing for modification of pricing rules without affecting other system components.
identifiedNFRs.justification: The complexity of fare calculations based on multiple variables requires a modular approach for easier maintenance and updates.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The system must support integration with at least 3 different payment gateways, with the ability to add new payment gateways without modifying the core payment processing logic.

functionalRequirement: The system shall generate a PDF report of all transactions and send a copy to the customer's email address and another copy to the system database for monthly transaction calculation.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The PDF report must include all transaction details including date, time, transaction ID, amount, payment method, and item details with 100% accuracy and completeness.
identifiedNFRs.justification: The FR requires comprehensive transaction reporting with no missing information to ensure functional completeness.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The system must generate the PDF report and send it to both the customer's email and the database within 30 seconds of transaction completion.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Timely generation and delivery of transaction reports is necessary for good user experience and operational efficiency.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The PDF generation process must consume no more than 100MB of memory per report, regardless of the number of transactions included.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Efficient resource utilization is important for scalability, especially when generating reports with many transactions.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The PDF report must be formatted with a clear hierarchical structure, consistent font sizes (minimum 11pt), appropriate spacing, and must be accessible according to PDF/UA standards.
identifiedNFRs.justification: The report needs to be easily readable and accessible to all users, including those with disabilities.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The system must successfully deliver email reports to customers for at least 99% of all transactions, with automatic retry mechanisms for failed deliveries (3 attempts at 10-minute intervals).
identifiedNFRs.justification: Reliable delivery of transaction reports is essential as they serve as receipts and records for customers.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: All PDF reports must be digitally signed to ensure authenticity and must be encrypted with AES-256 when stored in the database and when transmitted via email.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Transaction reports contain sensitive financial information requiring protection and verification of authenticity.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: Customer email addresses must be validated before sending reports and must be stored in the database using appropriate encryption or hashing techniques in compliance with data protection regulations.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Email addresses are personal data requiring protection, and validation prevents delivery errors.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The PDF report template must be configurable through external files or database settings, allowing for changes to report format, branding, and content without requiring code modifications.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Report formats often need updates for branding or content changes, requiring easy maintainability.

identifiedNFRs.requirement: The system must support multiple email service providers with automatic failover capability if the primary email service is unavailable.
identifiedNFRs.justification: Email delivery is critical to the FR, requiring adaptability to ensure successful delivery under various conditions.
